label: ERP field notes
title: Epicor, SyteLine & On-Premises ERP Guides | OPERIS
h1: More control over the systems you already run.
description: Practical guides to Epicor, Infor SyteLine, on-premises ERP, and read-only discovery for manufacturing teams planning their next improvement.

sections.heading: Start with the work between systems
paragraphs: An order can move through an ERP, a spreadsheet, an inbox, and several conversations before anyone knows why it is late. Understanding those handoffs is the starting point for a useful improvement.

OPERIS is being developed as an intelligence layer above existing business systems. These guides explain how to inventory dependencies, define access boundaries, and choose a first workflow. Connector availability and deployment fit require environment-specific validation.

label: Epicor planning
title: Epicor ERP Discovery & Integration Planning | OPERIS
h1: Understand your Epicor dependencies before the next change.
description: Plan Epicor discovery around your reports, customizations, integrations, and operational handoffs. Build an evidence base before an upgrade or migration.

sections.heading: Map the workflow people actually use
paragraphs: Start with one outcome: releasing a job, resolving an invoice exception, or explaining a late order. List each ERP screen, report, spreadsheet, and email used to reach that outcome. Record who owns the next step and which information they need.

A dependency inventory should capture the Epicor version, deployment model, companies and plants in scope, business-critical reports, custom logic, and integration owners. Document what is known separately from what still needs testing.

sections.heading: Keep the initial discovery scope read-only
items: Define the permitted metadata and business records before granting access.
Use a dedicated identity with only the approved permissions.
Measure query impact and agree a suitable scan window.
Record unavailable objects and access errors instead of claiming full coverage.
Keep source-system changes outside the initial assessment.

sections.heading: Make migration questions specific
paragraphs: Epicor identifies 2028.1 as its final on-premises feature release for Kinetic. That makes a documented dependency inventory useful now. A lifecycle announcement does not prove that any one customer's workflow will fail or establish the terms of their support agreement.
Ask how reporting, printing, file exchange, custom logic, and data extraction will work in the proposed environment. Validate the critical paths before making a deployment decision.

sections.heading: Where OPERIS fits
paragraphs: The planned OPERIS approach begins with discovery and evidence-linked recommendations. A first implementation should have a bounded workflow, a clear business owner, and measurable acceptance criteria. Epicor connectivity and source write-back are not established by this educational guide.

label: Infor SyteLine planning
title: Infor SyteLine & CloudSuite Industrial Discovery | OPERIS
h1: Map your Infor SyteLine and CloudSuite Industrial workflows.
description: A discovery guide for Infor SyteLine and CloudSuite Industrial teams assessing reports, customizations, data access, and manufacturing workflows.

sections.heading: Start with your exact environment
paragraphs: Prioritize the terms your team and vendor materials actually use: Infor SyteLine, CloudSuite Industrial, or both. Record the actual version, deployment, licensed capabilities, and extensions used by your organization. Similar product names do not establish identical integration behavior.
Choose one business process and map how information crosses reports, forms, external applications, and people. Separate documented interfaces from assumptions about how the environment works.

sections.heading: Questions for the system owner
items: Which reports are essential to daily production or financial reconciliation?
Which custom forms or extensions contain company-specific rules?
Who owns each interface, and how are failed transfers detected?
Which data can be accessed through approved interfaces in this version?
What changes when the deployment or update schedule changes?
How will a pilot prove source totals, permissions, and data freshness?

sections.heading: Use discovery to choose the first improvement
paragraphs: A first pilot might focus on visibility into one exception queue or the handoff between a report and a person. Define the expected source values, the permitted users, and the action that remains with the business owner.

Infor SyteLine and CloudSuite Industrial are target areas for OPERIS research and adapter planning. A production-ready OPERIS connector for either environment has not been verified in this foundation. These resources support evaluation; they are not a compatibility certification.

label: On-premises ERP
title: On-Premises ERP Control & Modernization | OPERIS
h1: Keep ERP deployment decisions grounded in operational requirements.
description: Evaluate on-premises, private hosting, and cloud ERP through data access, upgrade control, recovery, integrations, and the work your team must support.

sections.heading: Define what control means for your team
paragraphs: Control can mean deciding when to upgrade, understanding where copies of data live, exporting records in a useful form, or restoring service after a failure. Put those requirements in writing. The location of an ERP server alone does not answer them.

On-premises operation also assigns responsibilities to the customer: infrastructure, monitoring, backups, restoration, and maintenance. Cloud and managed hosting change those responsibilities. Compare the actual operating agreements and technical interfaces, not broad assumptions about either model.

sections.heading: Compare the full operating model
items: Data access: permitted interfaces, export format, frequency, and ownership of copies.
Updates: notice, test environment, regression checks, and recovery procedure.
Continuity: critical dependencies, restoration evidence, and outage procedures.
Integrations: file exchange, equipment links, reporting, and custom logic.
Cost: licensing, hosting, administration, testing, support, and transition effort.
People: named owners for daily operations and exception escalation.

sections.heading: Improve one layer at a time
paragraphs: Documenting the existing environment can reveal useful improvements before a major migration: fewer reconciliations, clearer exception ownership, or a report that consistently explains its source and freshness. Begin with observation and compare outputs against the ERP.

An ERP hosted on-premises does not imply that an attached analytics or AI service keeps all data on-premises. Review every processing and storage boundary. OPERIS local-only processing and deployment options must be validated before they are promised.

label: Discovery readiness checklist
title: Read-Only ERP Discovery Readiness Checklist | OPERIS
h1: Prepare for a useful ERP discovery assessment.
description: Use this checklist to document your ERP environment, read-only permissions, data boundaries, and the first workflow you want to improve.

sections.heading: 1. Identify the environment
items: ERP product, version, hosting arrangement, and test environment.
Companies, plants, and workflow domains included in the assessment.
System owner, business owner, and person authorized to approve access.

sections.heading: 2. Describe one problem
paragraphs: Write down the outcome that is difficult today, how often the problem occurs, and how the team handles it. A useful example is: every morning the planner reconciles two reports to identify orders waiting for material. Record the actual time and error baseline when available; do not substitute an estimate presented as a measured result.

sections.heading: 3. Establish read-only boundaries
items: Approved interfaces and a dedicated identity with limited permissions.
Metadata versus business-record scope, including excluded fields.
Where extracted information may be stored and processed, and for how long.
A scan window, query limits, a stop contact, and an access revocation procedure.
No operational writes during initial discovery.

sections.heading: 4. Agree what the assessment must return
items: An inventory of what was accessible and what was not.
Source-linked findings with uncertainty stated.
A dependency map covering systems and human handoffs.
A ranked opportunity list tied to the observed workflow.
A proposed first pilot with acceptance criteria and a named owner.

sections.heading: 5. Review the result before enabling actions
paragraphs: Compare the findings with system owners and reconcile the important totals. Treat write-back as a later, separate scope with permissions, tests, approvals, and recovery procedures.

This checklist is available to use now. A downloadable customer scanner, paid discovery checkout, and adapter availability require separate product verification; this page does not claim those services are live.

label: Epicor · Planning
title: Epicor On-Premises Planning: Map Dependencies | OPERIS
h1: Before your next Epicor decision, inventory the dependencies.
description: Build a practical inventory of Epicor reports, integrations, and workflow handoffs so your next deployment decision starts with evidence.

sections.heading: A deployment decision is also a workflow decision
paragraphs: The ERP application is only part of the environment a manufacturer relies on. A shipping decision might require a report, a label template, a file transfer, and knowledge held by one experienced employee. An inventory that lists only servers and licenses will miss those dependencies.

Epicor's current announcement identifies Kinetic 2028.1 as the final on-premises release to add new features. Customers should check the official guidance and their own agreements for the applicable support details. The practical next step is to establish what the business depends on today.

sections.heading: Choose a process with a clear finish line
paragraphs: Start with one repeatable outcome, such as releasing an order to production. Ask the process owner to walk through the last real example. Record every report, screen, spreadsheet, and conversation used. Include work performed outside Epicor, especially manual reconciliation and exception handling.

For each step, record an owner, the information read, the output produced, and the next recipient. Mark uncertain details as questions. A useful inventory preserves uncertainty so the team knows what still needs investigation.

sections.heading: Use six fields for each dependency
items: Business purpose: the outcome the dependency supports.
Source and destination: where information begins and ends.
Access method: the approved interface used in the current environment.
Owner: the person who can explain and test the behavior.
Failure impact: what stops, becomes delayed, or needs a workaround.
Acceptance evidence: the comparison that would establish correct behavior after a change.

sections.heading: Turn concerns into testable questions
paragraphs: Instead of asking whether cloud ERP will work, ask whether the critical production report returns the required fields within an acceptable time. Instead of assuming a customization will transfer unchanged, identify its dependencies and ask for a demonstration in the proposed environment.

A report can render successfully and still be operationally wrong. Check totals, filters, company scope, timestamps, and the treatment of exceptions. Include representative edge cases chosen by the people doing the work.

sections.heading: Make the first scan proportional to the question
paragraphs: An initial discovery exercise should have a defined read-only scope. Agree the interfaces, identities, record boundaries, query limits, and processing locations before it starts. Prefer a suitable test environment when available and assess the load of any production reads.

The result should explain both coverage and gaps. If an interface is unavailable, that is a finding to resolve, not permission to claim the scan covered the entire system. Keep credentials and exported customer information out of marketing materials.

sections.heading: Use the inventory to make a smaller first decision
paragraphs: The first decision may be to document a fragile handoff, improve one exception view, or test a single integration. It does not have to settle the entire deployment strategy. Prioritize an improvement with a measurable baseline, a named owner, and a way to compare results with the ERP.

OPERIS's proposed discovery approach follows this sequence: understand the environment, establish evidence, then define a bounded improvement. Adapter behavior and any later source writes require separate validation. Use the discovery readiness checklist to prepare the first conversation with your system owner.

label: On-premises · Data control
title: On-Premises ERP: What Data Control Means | OPERIS
h1: What does controlling your ERP data actually mean?
description: Use concrete questions about access, copies, processing, exports, and recovery to evaluate data control across on-premises and cloud ERP environments.

sections.heading: Begin with a map of the copies
paragraphs: A server inside the building does not provide a complete picture of where ERP information goes. Reports can be exported, attachments can move through email, backups can be hosted elsewhere, and analytics services can process selected records. To assess control, map those flows.

For one workflow, list the source record and every place it is copied or transformed. Include temporary exports and manual spreadsheets. Record the owner, purpose, access permissions, and retention expectations for each destination.

sections.heading: Separate access from recoverability
paragraphs: Being able to view a record is different from being able to export it in a useful form. Having a backup is different from demonstrating that the required application and data can be restored within an acceptable window. Ask for evidence of each capability independently.

A practical review starts with representative information from the selected workflow. Can an authorized user retrieve the fields, relationships, and attachments needed to explain the process? Can another qualified person interpret the export? Where must that person rely on undocumented knowledge?

sections.heading: Ask specific questions about connected services
items: Which fields leave the ERP, and what business purpose requires each one?
Where are transmitted data and diagnostic logs stored?
Which people and services can access those copies?
How are permissions revoked and retained copies handled?
Can processing be limited to metadata or a smaller approved dataset?
Which processing steps use external services, including AI providers?

sections.heading: Evaluate on-premises and hosted options consistently
paragraphs: Use the same requirements for every option under consideration. Document who patches infrastructure, tests updates, monitors failures, maintains backups, and restores service. Review the actual terms and configuration with the responsible providers and internal owners.

This comparison often reveals responsibilities that have no clear owner. An integration may have been reliable for years while its failure notifications go to a departed employee. That is a control gap regardless of where the ERP is hosted.

sections.heading: Start with observation before automation
paragraphs: A read-only discovery scope gives the team a way to understand relationships and gaps before authorizing operational changes. Read-only still requires care: data access, query load, and downstream copies must be bounded and documented.

Define the first output in terms the business can review. For example, produce a source-linked map of how an invoice exception reaches the person who resolves it. Compare the map with actual cases. Identify where ownership or evidence disappears.

sections.heading: Make control a requirement you can demonstrate
paragraphs: Replace a broad promise such as full data control with a specific requirement: the system owner can identify every processing destination for the approved dataset, revoke the discovery identity, and retrieve the resulting inventory in a usable format. Agree the acceptance evidence before connecting a tool.

OPERIS is being developed around discovery and governed improvements above existing systems. An on-premises ERP connection should never be taken as proof that all OPERIS processing stays on-premises. Validate the full data path for the proposed deployment. The readiness checklist provides a starting point for that review.
